title: A birth gift that grows up with them
body:
Why most baby gifts are gone within a year

New parents receive a mountain of clothes, cuddly toys and bibs. Almost all of it is lovely, and almost all of it is outgrown within months. The gifts that stay are the ones that are not about the baby's size, but about the baby's story: when and where it began.

What new parents really appreciate

  • Nothing to do. No assembly, no washing, no batteries.
  • Something calm. A nursery fills up quickly with bright colours. A quiet, beautiful object is welcome.
  • Something for later. A gift the child will one day ask about.

Six ideas that last

  1. A map of where they were born. The town, the neighbourhood or the street of the first home, with a star on the spot and the date of birth.
  2. A time capsule. A box with the newspaper of the day, a letter from you and a photo of the parents, to open on their eighteenth birthday.
  3. A book with a message inside. A children's classic you loved yourself, with a handwritten dedication on the first page.
  4. A savings account or a share. Unexciting today, very welcome in twenty years.
  5. A meal for the parents. Bring dinner in the first weeks. Nothing is appreciated more.
  6. A print of the first walk. The route the parents take with the pram, on a map of their neighbourhood.

How to make a birth map

1. Choose the place

The town of birth is the classic choice. You can also show the street of the house they will grow up in, close enough to recognise the park and the school around the corner.

2. Mark the spot

A small star on the hospital or on the house, depending on where the baby was born. A heart or a tree works beautifully too.

3. Add the details

  • The name of the baby
  • The date of birth, and the time if the parents like that
  • A line such as Where you were born or Welcome to the world

4. Colours for a nursery

Soft blues, sage green, sand and blush look calm and grow with the room. Avoid choosing a colour just because of pink or blue: a neutral palette still looks good when the nursery becomes a teenager's bedroom.

5. Size and frame

30×40 cm or 40×50 cm suits a nursery wall above the changing table or the cot. Choose a light wood or white frame for a soft look. See every option in our guide to sizes and frames.

When to give it

The first weeks after the birth are full of visits and full of gifts. A framed print is a lovely thing to bring along on a visit, or to have sent to the parents when the first rush is over. Every print is made to order close to them and usually arrives within 3 to 7 working days in Europe.

More inspiration for a new arrival: see our birth map prints.
summary: Babies outgrow the onesies in a month. Here is how to choose a birth gift that is still on the wall when they start school, with six ideas and a guide to a map of where they were born.
